lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Systems of Linear Equations and Inequalities
lessonRef.title: Concept model C: solving systems exactly and approximately

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example is written more briefly. Fill in the reasoning it leaves out.

items.prompt: How many solutions has 2x + y = 5 and 4x + 2y = 11?

steps: The lines are parallel and distinct.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Is the point (-2, 1) in the solution region of -1x − 3y ≤ 3?
choices: No; substituting gives -1, which is greater than 3.
Only points on the boundary line are in the solution region.
The region cannot be tested without graphing it first.
Yes; substituting gives -1 ≤ 3.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 3 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system is equivalent only when 3 is 1.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.
The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.
The new system may lose solutions that the original had.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt:
How many solutions does this system have?
  7x − 1y = 9
  28x − 4y = 36
choices: no solution
infinitely many solutions
exactly one solution
exactly two solutions

items.prompt: Is the point (4, 5) in the solution region of 8x + 1y ≤ -14?
choices: Only points on the boundary line are in the solution region.
No; substituting gives 37, which is greater than -14.
The region cannot be tested without graphing it first.
Yes; substituting gives 37 ≤ -14.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 4 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system may lose solutions that the original had.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.
The new system is equivalent only when 4 is 1.
The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt:
How many solutions does this system have?
  -2x + 6y = -5
  -8x + 24y = -20
choices: no solution
infinitely many solutions
exactly two solutions
exactly one solution
